findings.title: Scanner baseline signatures can never match real ubs output: they include an absolute path that depends on cwd and a GitHub blob URL that carries the sha and line number
findings.evidence: This confirms conductor fact 2 and is its first root cause. Setup: a disposable worktree at 40140a5 and a scratch dir built the way the gate builds it (git show 12419312:<f>). The HEAD scan was `ubs hooks/bead-capture-guard.py hooks/bead-capture-guard.test.py` from the repo root. Real HEAD DETAIL line: `/tmp/rv3.2ftz/hooks/bead-capture-guard.py:305  Possible unreachable code after return — return None (https://github.com/craigvandotcom/agent-compounds/blob/40140a5e.../hooks/bead-capture-guard.py#L305)`. Real base DETAIL line from the scratch dir: `/tmp/rv3base/hooks/bead-capture-guard.py:283  Possible unreachable code after return — return None`. ubs prints absolute paths. It appends the blob URL only inside a git repo, and the scratch dir is not one. sig_of keeps both the path and the message tail, so the two keys never agree. I fed the real outputs through the gate's own awk plus `grep -cxFf`: 0 of 5 HEAD sigs matched the 9 base sigs. After stripping the root prefix and the URL, 4 of 5 matched. The URL also embeds `#L<line>`, which contradicts the leg's own promise (line ~570) that it is 'never line number'.
findings.fix: Normalize each signature before comparing. Make the path relative to the scan root: strip `$PWD/` for HEAD and `$SCRATCH/` for base. Strip a trailing ` (https://…)` URL group from the message. Add a close-gate.test.sh case that replays captured real ubs output shapes: absolute path, URL suffix, path:line with no column.

findings.title: Summary-only findings are always counted new, so the pre-existing rescue can never pass a Python file with ruff/bandit findings or truncated details
findings.evidence: This is the second root cause of fact 2 (21 = 5 + 16). Real HEAD run: Combined Summary `Info: 21`. Only 5 DETAIL lines parse: the unreachable-code category prints `(8 found)` but shows 5, ruff's 13 findings are a JSON array, and bandit's use `Location:` lines. So HEAD_COUNT=5, SUM_TOTAL - HEAD_COUNT = 16, and the leg adds those 16 as new without condition. The base run had Warning 3 / Info 18 of its own summary-only findings, which the leg ignores. Even with the path/URL fix, re-closing ac-4y7l.2 would still refuse with at least 16 'new' findings. The rescue is dead for any Python file carrying ruff/bandit output, which is the population FRICTIONS scanner-leg-has-no-baseline is about.
findings.fix: Compare summary-only overflow against the base: new_overflow = max(0, (HEAD_SUM - HEAD_COUNT) - (BASE_SUM - BASE_COUNT)). Better: parse ruff's JSON (filename + name + message) and bandit's `>> Issue: [Bxxx]` + `Location:` path as signature sources, so fewer findings fall into the unmatched bucket.

findings.title: The base scan runs in a scratch dir without the repo's ruff.toml, so base and HEAD are scanned under different rule sets
findings.evidence: `BASE_OUT=$(cd "$SCRATCH" && ubs ...)`: the scratch holds only the scanned files. The repo root has ruff.toml (line-length 120, select E/F/W/I). Measured: the HEAD run emitted 12 `line-too-long` ruff findings and the base run emitted 0, with a different rule mix (shebang-not-executable, collapsible-if, multiple-starts-ends-with). So a finding the bead inherited can show as new only because the config changed, and a baseline finding may come from a rule HEAD does not run.
findings.fix: Copy the root lint configs (ruff.toml, pyproject.toml, .ubsignore, etc.) from BASE_TREE into SCRATCH before scanning. Or scan the base in a `git worktree add --detach` of BASE_TREE, which also gives both runs the same URL/path shape.

findings.title: Test fixture's mock ubs does not match real ubs output, which hid both scanner defects
findings.evidence: The `content` mode emits `   $f:$ln:1  finding ... — rule.$tok`. That is the relative path as passed, a :col field, no URL suffix, and `Critical: 0 / Warning: 0 / Info: 0` even while printing DETAIL lines. Real ubs (above) prints absolute paths, path:line only for these categories, a blob URL when inside git, and summary counters above the DETAIL count. Every mismatch sits exactly where the matcher breaks, so AC4b 'pre-existing does not refuse' passes (71/71) while the real re-close of ac-4y7l.2 refused 21/0. ac-4y7l.23's causal probe is `grep -qF 'pre-existing ubs finding does not refuse' … && bash close-gate.test.sh`, so its proof runs entirely against this mock.
findings.fix: Make the mock print `$(cd "$(dirname $f)" && pwd)/$(basename $f):$ln` with a ` (https://…#L$ln)` suffix when `git rev-parse` succeeds. Make the summary counters at least the DETAIL count, plus an overflow finding with no DETAIL line. Add one case replaying a captured real ubs transcript.

findings.title: refly.test.sh br mock drops --transition-comment, so 2 cases fail on the committed tree
findings.evidence: This confirms conductor fact 1. `bash skills/ac-implement/scripts/refly.test.sh` gives 18 passed, 2 failed: 'landed bead: no FRESH-VERIFY record' and 'cascade bead: no TRIAGE-CLOSE record'. Root cause: ac-4y7l.15 moved close-gate's landing record from `br_call comments add` to `br close … --transition-comment "$LND_TEXT"` (close-gate.sh ~line 724). The refly mock's `close)` branch only flips status and never writes the transition comment to BR_COMMENTS_LOG. close-gate.test.sh's own mock was updated; this second consumer of the same write path was not. Why it slipped through: .15's atomicity AC probe is `grep -q 'transition-comment' close-gate.sh` (it runs no test), and its other probes run only close-gate.test.sh. refly.test.sh, a known close-gate caller, was not in any probe. Real br 0.5.12 does write the record: real ac-4y7l.22/.23/.15 each carry a `GATE: receipt` comment, so this is a harness defect, not a product defect.
findings.fix: In the refly mock's close branch, parse `--transition-comment <text>` and append it to $BR_COMMENTS_LOG, mirroring close-gate.test.sh's mock. Add refly.test.sh (and every other suite whose br shim handles `close`) to the probe set of any bead that changes close-gate's write path.

findings.title: Set-membership match rescues a newly added duplicate finding
findings.evidence: `printf '%s\n' "$BASE_SIGS" | grep -qxF "$s"` tests each HEAD sig for presence in base, not for count. Line numbers are dropped by design, so the same code text gives identical sigs. Real data shows this is common: HEAD has two `Possible unreachable code after return — return None` findings (lines 305, 308) and so does base (283, 286). With one base occurrence and three at HEAD, all three count as pre-existing and the bead's new ones pass silently.
findings.fix: Match as a multiset: count occurrences per sig in base and at HEAD, and count max(0, head_n - base_n) as new. For example: `sort | uniq -c` both sides, then join.

findings.title: An earlier unauthorized DECISION line permanently masks a later valid human ruling
findings.evidence: `grep -m1 -E '^DECISION \(...' ` picks the FIRST comment first-line shaped like a ruling, and only that one is authorized. Take a bead where an agent wrote `DECISION (agent): …` (the shape human-gate-template.md lines 60/78 tell agents to record) or `DECISION (ac-tidy): moot` without the pipeline-proposal label, and Craig later adds `DECISION (Craig): …`. RULING is set to the agent line, AUTHORIZED stays 0, and the close is refused forever. Comments are append-only, so no action frees the bead. The refusal message does not name the actor it rejected either. Related: human-gate-template.md:226, the canon worked example, still shows `DECISION (operator): …`, which the gate now refuses because 'operator' is not on `Humans who rule: Craig`.
findings.fix: Loop over all first-line DECISION candidates and accept the first authorized one. Name the rejected actor(s) in CLOSE-REFUSED DECISION. Change the human-gate-template.md example to `DECISION (Craig): …`.
